target.name: Lumina Vehicles
target.founder: Ahmed Shubber (CEO; Fairfield U double-major mech + biomedical eng), Federico Di Palma (Co-founder)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $8M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Lumina Vehicles is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ahmed Shubber (CEO) and Federico Di Palma, having raised $8M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—alongside a broader ecosystem of 9 private and 1 public robotics firm.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis anchors to the $8M total raised and applies a standard 2.0x Series A forward multiplier, implying a $16M valuation. The peer-median method uses the 4-company comparable set, which demonstrates a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer group: three Series B firms cluster between $1.6B–$2.0B, while one Seed-stage peer sits at $1.1B.

The triangulated range spans $14M (stage-progression low) to $2.0B (peer high), with a median of $858M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects the stage discount implicit in Lumina's Series A status relative to later-stage comparables. Key uncertainties include team execution capability, capital efficiency relative to peers, and whether peer valuations represent sustainable multiples in a maturing robotics sector.
